newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek court upholds seizure of ex-king's property.
newsitem.headline: Greek court upholds seizure of ex-king's property.

text.p: Greece's Supreme Special Court ruled on Tuesday that a 1994 law under which the property of former king Constantine was seized was constitutional and that thousands of acres of land would return to the Greek state.
Court officials said the 13-member tribunal voted nine to four to seize forest land in Tatoi outside Athens, in Polydendri, central Greece and the Mon Repos estate on the island of Corfu.
A Socialist bill passed by parliament in April 1994 seized all property owned by Constantine and his family in Greece and stripped the former royals of their Greek passports.

Constantine, 56, fought the case in court claiming the law was unconstitutional and after two different decisions -- one backing Constantine and one against him by two different tribunals -- the Supreme Special Court made the final ruling.
Constantine cannot appeal the decision and has said he would take his case to the European court of human rights.
Constantine has lived in England since fleeing Greece in December 1967 after a failed attempt to overthrow a military junta that had seized power earlier that year.
A referendum in 1974 abolished the monarchy in Greece.
